title: Summary of Benefits — Covered Failures, Exclusions and Waiting Periods across Northloop Protect Plans
content:
The Northloop Protect Plans fall into two families. The Extended Warranty plans cover mechanical failure and power surge; the Accident Protection plans cover those two failure types and also accidental damage, liquid damage and cracked screens. The table below sets out, plan by plan, the covered failure types, the exclusions, the waiting periods and whether mechanical failures within the manufacturer's warranty period go to the manufacturer first.

## Coverage by plan

| Term | 1-Year Extended Warranty | 2-Year Extended Warranty | 3-Year Extended Warranty | 2-Year Accident Protection | 3-Year Accident Protection | 4-Year Accident Protection |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Covered failure types | Mechanical failure, power surge | Mechanical failure, power surge | Mechanical failure, power surge | Mechanical failure, power surge, accidental damage, liquid damage, cracked screen | Mechanical failure, power surge, accidental damage, liquid damage, cracked screen | Mechanical failure, power surge, accidental damage, liquid damage, cracked screen |
| Theft or loss | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered |
| Cosmetic damage that does not affect function | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered |
| Battery that no longer holds a charge | Not covered | Covered | Covered | Not covered | Covered | Covered |
| Failures existing before coverage start | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered |
| Items used commercially | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered | Not covered |
| Waiting period for a mechanical failure or power surge incident | 30 calendar days after coverage start | 30 calendar days after coverage start | 30 calendar days after coverage start | 30 calendar days after coverage start | 30 calendar days after coverage start | 30 calendar days after coverage start |
| Waiting period for an accident incident | Not applicable (no accident cover) | Not applicable (no accident cover) | Not applicable (no accident cover) | 0 calendar days | 0 calendar days | 0 calendar days |
| Mechanical failures within the manufacturer's warranty period sent to the manufacturer first | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

All six plans are printed in the table under their family names; in full they are Protect 1-Year Extended Warranty, Protect 2-Year Extended Warranty, Protect 3-Year Extended Warranty, Protect 2-Year Accident Protection, Protect 3-Year Accident Protection and Protect 4-Year Accident Protection.

## Notes on the summary

**Waiting periods.** A waiting period is counted in calendar days after the coverage start. A mechanical failure or power surge incident is covered only once the 30 calendar days have passed, on every plan. On the Accident Protection plans the accident waiting period is 0 calendar days, so an accident incident is covered from the coverage start; the Extended Warranty plans have no accident cover, so no accident waiting period applies to them.

**Battery cover differs within each family.** Protect 1-Year Extended Warranty and Protect 2-Year Accident Protection do not cover a battery that no longer holds a charge; the other four plans do.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- Coverage on a Protect 3-Year Accident Protection plan starts on a given day. Liquid damage on the second day of coverage is within the plan's covered failure types and has a 0-day accident waiting period. A mechanical failure on the tenth day of coverage falls inside the 30-day waiting period and is not covered; a mechanical failure on the fiftieth day is past it.
- A battery that no longer holds a charge is not covered on Protect 1-Year Extended Warranty and is covered on Protect 2-Year Extended Warranty.
- A cracked screen is not a covered failure type on any Extended Warranty plan.
